newsitem.title: UK: New UK government must weaken sterling - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: New UK government must weaken sterling - newspaper.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government has to adopt policies that will gradually drive down the pound to avoid economic damage to the country, the Times newspaper said in a column on Friday. "The new goverment must create the conditions for an immediate fall in the pound," Times writer Anatole Kaletsky said in his "Economic View" column.

By putting in place policies now that will gradually ease the pound, the government can pre-empt a much bigger devaluation that will otherwise become inevitable in one or two years' time, the paper said.

"By expressing his desire for a lower pound and backing it up with some Bank of England currency intervention, (finance minister-in-waiting Gordon) Brown could send an immediate signal to currency traders to start taking the big profits that they have built up by buying the pound," Kaletsky wrote.

Taxes will have to go up in the new government's first budget so the pressure for interest rates to rise can be eased, the paper said. A quarter-point rise in interest rates at the next monetary meeting is a foregone conclusion, it said.

"In raising base rates next week, ..., Brown should make clear that tighter monetary policy is only a temporary expedient to control the economy until the budget can put it on the right track," the Times said.
